name: Complete Wing-Back 4-2-3-1

slots.why: Sweeper keeper is an extra passer in build-up and covers the space behind a higher line.
Complete wing-back (Attack) overlaps the playmaker on the left and gets in crosses and passes.
Ball-playing defender starts moves with passes into midfield.
Central defender who defends while his partner plays. Cover is the alternate.
Complete wing-back (Support) is the more cautious of the two, staying back more so one flank is safer.
Holding midfielder protects the back line and covers the flank when the wing-back goes forward.
Ball-winning midfielder wins the ball back, starts the counter-press and helps cover the wide areas.
Playmaker on the left drifts inside and creates from the half-space, which leaves the flank to the wing-back.
Advanced playmaker (Support) is the creative centre and links the flanks.
Inverted winger (Attack) cuts in from the right to shoot and attack the far post.
Deep-lying forward (Attack) links play but also runs at the defence, so the striker is not only a passer.

description: A 4-2-3-1 with two complete wing-backs who provide both the width and the creativity from the flanks, supported by playmakers inside them and a striker who drops to link play.
whyGood: Wing-backs who can cross, pass and dribble overload the flank against the opposition full-back, and the playmakers inside them give the team several ways to reach the box.
whyThisShape: Both flanks are overloaded: on the left the complete wing-back overlaps a playmaker who drifts inside, and on the right the wing-back supports an inside forward who cuts in. The double pivot stays behind them to cover the flanks when the wing-backs go forward, so the team attacks with width and stays protected.
whenToUse: When your two full-backs are among your best attacking players, or against a team that defends narrowly and leaves the flanks open.
whenNotToUse: Against quick wingers, if your wing-backs cannot recover; or when the double pivot cannot cover the flanks.

instructionRationale.Shorter Passing: Use the short connections supplied by the selected midfield and supporting forwards.
instructionRationale.Play Out Of Defence: Use short first-line outlets and midfield connections to start attacks; this asks for secure decisions under pressure.
instructionRationale.Work Ball Into Box: Look for an opening around the penalty area rather than encouraging speculative shots.
instructionRationale.Overlap Left: Ask the left-sided receiver to consider the outside run; this requires a wide defender who can supply that run.
instructionRationale.Counter-Press: Challenge immediately after losing possession, with the roles around the ball supporting the first pressure.
instructionRationale.Higher Line of Engagement: Engage the build-up earlier, accepting that the forwards need support from the midfield behind them.
instructionRationale.Distribute To Centre Backs: The selected outlets match where this tactic starts its build-up or releases pressure.
instructionRationale.Fairly Wide: Give the wide outlets space to receive and stretch the opponent without isolating every central passer.
instructionRationale.Low Crosses: A starting delivery choice for the receiving roles, to review against the actual forwards.
instructionRationale.More Urgent Pressing: Challenge more often inside the selected engagement zone without making the settled press maximal.
instructionRationale.Never Time Wasting: The kick-off baseline; review deliberately when score and time justify a different policy.
instructionRationale.Standard Defensive Line: Keep the back line at its mentality-relative default rather than explicitly pushing it up or dropping it.
instructionRationale.Take Short Kicks: Start possession through the chosen short outlets instead of routinely contesting a long kick.

keyRequirements: Two complete wing-backs with stamina and skill
Playmakers on the left and in the middle
A double pivot to cover the flanks
setupNotes: All three phases have been reviewed. Standard sliders are relative to the chosen mentality; unselected toggles intentionally leave FM to choose the response.
Player instructions use the selected role and duty defaults unless additional instructions are listed. Crossing and overlap settings are starting choices to review against the selected players.
